credential_reference.decision: Firstmate decision (review round 2, authorization-header-in-plain-grant): literal credentials are forbidden in the 0444 grant file and in any execute/helper argv. The typed HTTP request carries a reference to an owner-only credential file (canonical path plus sha256 of its bytes) bound into request_sha256 with the account and approved request; the executor resolves and checks that file at execution and places its value only in the in-memory Authorization header. Raw Authorization material in a request refuses with no fallback. This is a bounded extension of the existing typed HTTP adapter, not a credential broker or privileged service. Synthetic only; no host permissions, sudo or real credentials were touched.

before.method: Component capture separate from the original accepted binding BEFORE captures above: synthetic request with headers.Authorization 'Bearer SYNTHETIC_APPROVED' minted through the request codec; the payload-policy function then run with a python3 shim recording every helper argv.
before.verdict: FAIL: the old binding persisted the synthetic credential in the grant and repeated it as a helper argument

after.method: Same component path with an owner-only 0600 credential file holding 'Bearer SYNTHETIC_CREDENTIAL_SECRET', referenced by canonical path and sha256; a synthetic loopback endpoint recorded the Authorization header it received.
